title: Decision: string-based algo/provider names, no enums, no flags
description: Algorithm identification is by string name ('cbc(aes)', 'sha256'). Provider identification by string ('wolfssl', 'kcapi'). New behaviors get new ioctls, never flag bits. This is correct: (1) open namespace — adding AES-XTS requires no header change; (2) no combinatorial state — flag bits create untestable combinations; (3) audit clarity — a CMVP reviewer reads the UAPI header and immediately understands algorithm coverage. A reviewer suggesting 'use an enum for algo type to be type-safe' would create a closed namespace requiring a header update and recompile for every new algorithm. Do not let anyone add a flags field to any ioctl struct.
close_reason: Reviewed, documented, and hardened in CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, and AGENTS.md
